findings.description: Windows subprocess.Popen call in `dotenv run` CLI executes a command supplied by the CLI operator — intended functionality, shell=False, no untrusted input
findings.code_snippet: p = Popen(command, universal_newlines=True, bufsize=0, shell=False, env=cmd_env)
findings.reasoning: The `run` command's entire documented purpose is "Run command with environment variables present" — the command line is captured via `@click.argument("commandline", nargs=-1, type=click.UNPROCESSED)` and handed to `run_command()`. The command list originates from the local user invoking `dotenv run <cmd>` (i.e., the same principal who could type the command directly), so there is no trust boundary crossing and no privilege escalation. On Windows the invocation uses `Popen(command, ..., shell=False)` with an argument list, so shell metacharacters are not interpreted; there is no string concatenation of the .env values into the command. Values loaded from the .env file only populate the child environment (`env=cmd_env`), which does not enable command injection. No `shell=True`, no `os.system`, no `popen`. This is expected CLI behavior, not a vulnerability.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: Source = click.argument('commandline', nargs=-1, type=click.UNPROCESSED) supplied by the process owner on the local console. Sink = Popen(..., shell=False). No shell interpretation, argument list form, no injection of .env-derived data into the argv.
evidence.notes: No remote/attacker-controlled input path exists in this CLI module; it is not imported by the library runtime path (only the console_scripts entry point).

findings.description: os.execvpe in `dotenv run` replaces the process with the user-supplied command from the local CLI invocation — intended behavior, no shell, no untrusted input
findings.reasoning: `os.execvpe` is invoked with the argv list originating from the `dotenv run` command line, which is chosen by the same human operator running the CLI. `execvpe` does not spawn a shell, so shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$()`) are inert; it only performs a PATH lookup for argv[0]. The .env file influences only the environment dictionary. There is no path by which a third party (e.g. an attacker controlling a .env file) gains code execution beyond what they already have by controlling the process invocation — and env-var-only influence cannot redirect the executable because PATH is taken from the inherited environment (a .env entry named PATH would update cmd_env before exec, but that still cannot inject commands, and controlling PATH already implies control over the invoking user/session). Not a vulnerability in this library.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: command = click UNPROCESSED argument tuple from the invoking user -> run_command() -> os.execvpe(argv list). No shell=True, no string interpolation of dotsenv values into argv.
evidence.notes: The 'run' subcommand is a documented feature (equivalent to `env $(cat .env) cmd`); CodeQL's generic 'subprocess call' heuristic flags it, but there is no injected/untrusted data reaching the argv.

findings.description: Query flags Popen in dotenv's `run` CLI subcommand as potential OS command injection, but the call uses an argv list with shell=False.
findings.code_snippet:
if sys.platform == "win32":
        # execvpe on Windows returns control immediately
        # rather than once the command has finished.
        p = Popen(command, universal_newlines=True, bufsize=0, shell=False, env=cmd_env)
        _, _ = p.communicate()
findings.reasoning: `Popen` is invoked with `shell=False` and `command` as a list (from the click.UNPROCESSED nargs=-1 argument of the `run` command). Because no shell is spawned, there is no metacharacter interpretation, no word splitting and no glob expansion, so the classic CWE-78 injection vector does not exist. Furthermore, executing the operator-supplied command is the documented, intended behavior of `dotenv run` (it is the local user's own command line), so there is no privilege or trust boundary crossing. The `env=cmd_env` parameter passes `.env` values as environment variables (a dict), not as part of a command string, so untrusted `.env` file content cannot influence command execution.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: grep for 'shell=True' returned no matches anywhere in the repository. grep for 'Popen' shows exactly one call site (line 213) plus the import at line 9. No string concatenation, %-formatting, .format(), or shlex.split of user input into a command string anywhere in the sink path.
evidence.notes: This is the CLI tool 'python-dotenv[cli]' whose `run` subcommand is explicitly documented as 'Run command with environment variables present.' Executing a caller-provided command with shell=False and an argv list is the secure implementation pattern recommended for subprocess usage.

findings.description: Query flags os.execvpe in dotenv's `run` CLI subcommand as potential OS command injection; it is intentional argv-based execution of the user's own command.
findings.reasoning: `os.execvpe(file=command[0], args=command, env=cmd_env)` passes an explicit argv list and never invokes a shell, so no shell metacharacter interpretation, globbing or word-splitting can occur. `command` originates directly from the click `commandline` argument with type `click.UNPROCESSED`, meaning it is exactly the user's own command line for the documented `dotenv run -- <cmd>` feature. There is no injection into a command string and `env=cmd_env` only carries `.env` key/values as environment variables, which cannot alter the executed argv.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: Source: click @click.argument('commandline', nargs=-1, type=click.UNPROCESSED) in the `run` command -> run_command(commandline, dotenv_as_dict) -> os.execvpe(command[0], args=command, env=cmd_env). The path contains no shell invocation and no string interpolation, so the 'flow' is simply argv passthrough by design.
evidence.notes: Environment values from the .env file are only placed into the child environment dict; they are not used to build the command. Therefore a malicious .env file cannot achieve command injection through this code path. Note the broader (non-CodeQL) consideration: `dotenv run` will load arbitrary env vars from a .env file into a child process — expected behavior of the tool.

findings.reasoning: Location 214 is the `p.communicate()` attribute access on the Popen object created at line 213. Popen is called with an argv LIST (`command`), `shell=False`, and an explicit `env` dict. `command` originates from a click argument declared with `nargs=-1, type=click.UNPROCESSED`, i.e., the local operator names the program to exec. There is no shell metacharacter interpretation, no string concatenation, and no use of shell=True anywhere in the file. dotenv values only enter the child environment via the `env=` mapping, so even a hostile .env file cannot inject into a command line. This is the documented, intended behavior of `dotenv run` (equivalent to `env $(cat .env) cmd`), so no command-injection vulnerability exists.
